key_insight: Dementia-Agents uses a multi-agent workflow to turn heterogeneous clinical records into syndrome-level dementia staging and phenotyping, rather than only detecting Alzheimer’s disease.
clinical_relevance: This approach is designed to better reflect real-world dementia assessment, where clinicians must integrate incomplete multi-modal information across different informants and specialist domains.
method: A data agent converts structured records into semantically faithful text while preserving missing-data signals.
Five fine-tuned expert agents make domain-specific predictions.
A coordinator agent probabilistically combines expert outputs into the final staging/phenotyping decision.
evidence_signal: The system was evaluated on 1,066 patients from two cognitive neurology services and outperformed monolithic MLLMs and prior medical multi-agent systems on real-world syndrome-level dementia tasks.
watch_item: Because it depends on multi-agent orchestration and clinical record translation, performance and interpretability may vary when deployed in settings with different documentation quality, workflows, or patient populations.
paper_title: Dementia-Agents: A Multi-Modal Multi-Agent System for Dementia Staging and Phenotyping
